items.title: Ati Robotics adopts SimScale AI simulation for autonomous vehicle development
items.summary: Ati Robotics is using SimScale's AI-native cloud simulation technology to validate the hardware of its Sherpa autonomous mobile robot. The engineering team employs SimScale for structural and mechanical simulations of the platform to ensure it meets factory-floor operational requirements. This virtual testing allows for hardware performance investigation without the overhead of traditional simulation setups. SimScale also provides a shared simulation environment for engineering teams operating in the US and India. This adoption aligns with the broader manufacturing trend toward increased automation to address labor shortages and boost efficiency.

Furthermore, SimScale provides a shared simulation environment accessible to engineering teams operating in both the United States and India. This adoption reflects a broader manufacturing trend toward increased automation to address labor shortages and boost overall efficiency in the sector. This move signifies a progression in using advanced simulation for physical robotics validation. The industry should observe further integration of cloud-based simulation for hardware development.

items.title: ASRock Industrial launches ‘robotics-in-a-box’ for physical AI development
items.summary: ASRock Industrial launched the RBK-100 Robotics-in-a-Box to simplify physical AI development for researchers and developers. This integrated platform is powered by the ASRock Industrial NUC BOX-358H featuring an Intel Core Ultra X7 Processor 358H. It includes an RGB depth camera, a 6-DOF robotic arm, and AiRoboStarter software for hands-on experimentation. The system facilitates AI-based pick-and-place tasks, data collection, and model training in a unified workflow. Optionally, it supports agentic AI integration for multimodal robotic workflows.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, ASRock Industrial launched the RBK-100 Robotics-in-a-Box to simplify physical artificial intelligence development. This integrated platform provides researchers and developers with a unified system for hands-on experimentation with physical AI tasks. The system incorporates the ASRock Industrial NUC BOX-358H equipped with an Intel Core Ultra X7 Processor 358H, alongside an RGB depth camera, a six-degrees-of-freedom robotic arm, and AiRoboStarter software. This setup enables the execution of AI-based pick-and-place operations, data collection, and model training within a single workflow. The platform also offers the optional capability for agentic AI integration to support multimodal robotic workflows. This development points toward more accessible methods for bridging the gap between software AI and physical robotic execution.

items.title: Coprod raises $6 million to make ‘robot hardware as easy to build as software’
items.summary: Coprod raised $6 million in a pre-seed round to simplify building robotic hardware by focusing on compatible "co:products." The company aims to reduce the time and cost of robotics development, which is often hindered by complex component integration. Their hardware components work with a unified software API to standardize communication and maintain real-time performance. The funding will support bringing initial components to market and establishing a hardware prototyping facility. Coprod seeks to resolve "integration hell" in robotics by providing purpose-built, easy-to-use hardware.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, Coprod raises six million dollars in a pre-seed round to make robot hardware as easy to build as software. The company is focused on simplifying the construction of robotic hardware by concentrating on compatible co:products. This effort aims to reduce the time and expense associated with robotics development, which is frequently impeded by complex component integration. The hardware components utilize a unified software application programming interface to standardize communication and ensure real-time performance across the system. The raised funds will be allocated to launching initial components and setting up a facility for hardware prototyping. Coprod intends to alleviate integration challenges in robotics by supplying hardware designed for ease of use. This development signals a push toward more streamlined and accessible physical realization of complex robotic systems.

items.title: Yarbo opens SDK beta to developers for modular yard robots
items.summary: Yarbo has opened a closed beta for its Software Development Kit (SDK) to enable custom applications for its modular yard robots. This SDK is part of Yarbo's Open Platform strategy, which aims to allow users to customize robot interactions beyond hardware attachments. Developers can create applications and plugins to connect Yarbo devices with external systems like smart home platforms and commercial software. Potential uses include integrating mowing data with irrigation, coordinating snow removal, and supporting academic research on autonomous navigation. The SDK is a step toward an open robotics ecosystem that will eventually include a hardware development kit.

The development signals an expansion in how modular robotics are integrated into broader technological applications.

items.title: Figure AI patents wearable system for teaching humanoid robots through human movement
items.summary: Figure AI patented a wearable robotic system to capture human arm movements for training or remotely controlling humanoid robots. The system uses a backpack frame with articulated arms equipped with sensors to measure movements at the shoulder, elbow, and wrist. It is designed to capture data from everyday tasks in working environments without requiring motion-capture studios. The technology allows for real-time control with less than 20 milliseconds of delay. This system offers an alternative for collecting real-world training data for robotics by capturing demonstrations from human workers.

items.title: MassRobotics to open marine robotics facility at Boston Fish Pier
items.summary: MassRobotics is developing a new marine robotics facility at Boston Fish Pier to provide startups with access to Boston Harbor for testing underwater robots. This development is a partnership with Massport as part of the Blue Edge initiative to support the marine technology sector. Construction is underway, with the facility slated to open in early 2028, and industry programming will begin in 2027. The site will allow companies to design and test prototypes using existing workshops before entering the harbor. This facility aims to establish Boston as a global center for marine robotics and support the Marine Tech Hub initiative.

items.title: ABB launches ‘world’s first’ industrial motor with built-in AI
items.summary: ABB launched Intelleqt, the world's first low-voltage motor with integrated AI to provide real-time operational insights. This solution offers equipment-level intelligence, enabling customers to connect motor data to existing digital platforms. Intelleqt helps build the data foundation necessary for scaling AI-driven operations in industries. By providing insights, the technology can improve reliability, boost productivity, and reduce unplanned downtime. ABB plans a broader rollout for Intelleqt starting in 2027 across several international markets.

items.title: ROS Discourse General: MOLA cloud: free online LiDAR SLAM from ROS bags, plus camera and LiDAR-camera calibration
items.summary: MOLA cloud is a free web service that allows users to perform LiDAR SLAM and camera calibration directly in the browser using ROS 2 data. Users can upload ROS 2 bags to download 3D maps and input videos or image sets to derive camera intrinsics. The service automates the process of extracting point cloud maps, trajectory data, and extrinsic LiDAR-camera calibration. It supports various input formats and provides tools for viewing and further processing the resulting maps. The service operates on secure, isolated servers within the EU and enforces monthly usage limits.
items.audio_script: From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: MOLA cloud: free online LiDAR SLAM from ROS bags, plus camera and LiDAR-camera calibration". This report details the launch of MOLA cloud, a free online service enabling LiDAR SLAM and camera calibration directly within a web browser utilizing ROS 2 data. The service allows users to upload ROS 2 bags to generate three-dimensional maps and process video or image sets to derive camera intrinsics. It automates the extraction of point cloud maps, trajectory data, and the extrinsic LiDAR-camera calibration through an automated methodology. The service operates on secure, isolated servers within the European Union and implements monthly usage restrictions. This advancement offers a readily accessible method for complex spatial data processing and sensor fusion for developers. Further development in this area indicates increased accessibility to advanced robotics data processing tools.

items.title: How does Orchard AI fit into John Deere’s technology portfolio?
items.summary: John Deere acquired Orchard AI to integrate plant-level crop insights into its technology portfolio. Orchard AI uses AI-powered cameras to analyze individual plants, providing detailed data on yield, fruit, and canopy. This acquisition allows John Deere to combine crop intelligence with its precision agriculture equipment and technology. The goal is to help growers make more informed decisions by connecting crop-level intelligence with field execution capabilities. This move reflects John Deere's ongoing focus on integrating advanced AI into its offerings.

items.title: Viabot expands autonomous outdoor cleaning operations across eight US states
items.summary: Viabot is expanding its autonomous outdoor cleaning operations across eight US states using its Viabot One platform. This platform services 25 million square feet of commercial property, including shopping centers and university campuses. The robots use cameras, lidar, and GPS for autonomous navigation, debris collection, and property monitoring. The system features autonomous tool swapping and battery replacement, enabling 12 to 24 hours of operation. The company recently secured $24 million in Series A funding to support further expansion of its robotics-as-a-service business.

items.title: Samsung humanoid targets CES 2027 debut with 40 hand motors
items.summary: Samsung plans to debut its first humanoid robot at CES 2027, featuring 40 hand motors, to target smartphone assembly tasks. The robot's hands utilize a direct drive mechanism and joint technology adapted from Galaxy hinges. Development is led by the Hand Lab, resulting in two models: HR and HE. This humanoid aims to integrate into factory automation for production equipment management and assembly by 2030. A significant investment of 19 trillion won is planned for a humanoid mass production system and data infrastructure in Gumi.

Development is being led by the Hand Lab, which has utilized a direct drive mechanism and joint technology adapted from Galaxy hinges for the robot's hands. Two models, designated HR and HE, are in development, with the goal of integrating the humanoid into factory automation for production equipment management and assembly by the year 2030. A substantial investment of nineteen trillion won is allocated for establishing a humanoid mass production system and necessary data infrastructure in Gumi. This initiative signals a focused effort by Samsung to advance physical robotics within the industrial automation sector.

items.title: Flying race cars take to the skies as Airspeeder partners with Advanced Navigation
items.summary: Airspeeder is launching a racing series featuring electric flying cars capable of over 120 km/h, controlled remotely via augmented reality. Advanced Navigation has partnered with Airspeeder to provide the necessary precision positioning and flight control technology. The inaugural race is scheduled for November 2026 in Adelaide, Australia, with five international pilots participating. Competitors will navigate virtual racetracks superimposed on real-world environments in three dimensions. This collaboration also serves as an experimental ground for developing autonomous aviation technologies.

items.title: Schindler escalators provide mountain access at 2,300 meters in China
items.summary: Six Schindler escalators have provided access to Longtoushan's scenic peaks, located over 2,300 meters above sea level, for seven years. These outdoor escalators address significant accessibility challenges posed by harsh mountain weather, including heavy snowfall and low temperatures. The system, spanning approximately 170 meters, allows visitors to reach the summit while enjoying panoramic views. Schindler incorporated anti-freezing and heating systems to ensure reliable operation in the extreme climate. The project demonstrates how vertical transportation technology improves access to remote, challenging environments.

The outdoor escalator system, approximately 170 meters in length, was implemented to address accessibility difficulties in the harsh mountain environment characterized by heavy snowfall and low temperatures. Schindler integrated specific anti-freezing and heating systems into the apparatus to maintain reliable operation in the extreme climate. This project illustrates the application of vertical transportation technology in creating access to remote and challenging environments. This development signals advancements in engineering solutions for extreme environment accessibility.

items.title: A Dozen Completely DIY Robot Actuators
items.summary: Koshiro Robot created a dozen custom robot actuator motors, including their drivers and Field-Oriented Control (FOC) firmware. These actuators were designed for easy assembly and mounting, featuring a 3D-printed gearbox and motor controller outside the stator for better cooling and wiring simplicity. The design incorporates CAN-bus-plus-XT-60 daisy chaining for power and signal distribution. This approach multiplies cost savings by creating multiple units. The project demonstrates an experimentalist-friendly approach to reducing the cost of robot components.
items.audio_script: From Hackaday - Robots, "A Dozen Completely DIY Robot Actuators" reports on the creation of a set of custom robot actuator motors. The project demonstrates a methodology for significantly reducing the cost of robot components through modular design. The development involved Koshiro Robot creating a dozen custom robot actuator motors, complete with their drivers and Field-Oriented Control firmware. These actuators feature a 3D-printed gearbox and motor controller situated outside the stator to facilitate improved cooling and simplified wiring. Power and signal distribution are managed via CAN-bus-plus-XT-60 daisy chaining. This design strategy allows for cost multiplication by producing multiple identical units efficiently. This work showcases an experimentalist-friendly approach to lowering the expense of robotic hardware. The successful implementation suggests a pathway for democratizing access to cost-effective robotic components in future developments.

items.title: Figure and T-Mobile Bring F.03 Humanoids to the Las Vegas Grand Prix
items.summary: Figure partnered with T-Mobile to bring its F.03 humanoids to the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The robots were featured on the circuit and in the pit lane wearing co-branded vests. Footage showed the robots walking the track and pit lane, displaying the event and company logos. Specific details regarding the robots' role for fans and the commercial terms of the partnership were not disclosed. The appearance of the robots in this setting marks a shift from their previous demonstrations in industrial and residential settings.
